basics.name: Alvin Ferdinand
basics.label: Backend & Data Integration Engineer
basics.summary: Backend developer from Semarang who builds and looks after systems that teams use every day: an ERP, a 78-branch retail POS, an HR and recruitment system, and the integration between Odoo, Accurate Online and BigQuery. Most of my work sits where business data has to be right, so I check results against the source instead of trusting them. I also handle the security and server side of what I build, and I have connected the ERP to Claude through an MCP server.

work.name: PT Gosyen Solusi Indonesia (GSI Group)
highlights: Built the sync that moves daily transactions from Odoo 19 into Accurate Online: purchase orders, goods receipts, vendor bills, deliveries, sales invoices and down payments. It only reads from Odoo and enters each document in Accurate the way an admin would by hand.
Wrote checkers that compare every synced document with Odoo each day. All 79 purchase orders match, and payables, receivables and VAT equal Odoo on every invoice, with every journal balanced.

Covered the messy cases: edits made after posting, cancelled orders, document numbers reused by an older company, prices that include VAT with line discounts, and Odoo going down mid-run. Documents are posted the next morning so same-day edits land once.
Set up Accurate's chart of accounts to match Odoo's 64 accounts, so revenue lands on the same accounts in both systems.

When cost of goods would not match, I scanned all 4,482 items and 2,594 item-warehouse stock positions and showed management the real cause: duplicate items and stock split across codes. I handed over the evidence in a workbook with a risk list.
Built the Accurate-to-BigQuery data pipeline and a FIFO cost engine that matched 963 of 963 documents; the old spreadsheet matched 49.
Built the HR recruitment system and the public job portal, from applicant intake to onboarding (see Projects).

Built the inventory Android app (React Native with a Go API): QR asset scanning, loans, repair reports and fuel claims with approvals. Shipped it as APK releases that install on both 32-bit and 64-bit phones.
Built the company OKR system used to set and track objectives, key results and KPIs per division (see Projects).
Wrote automated tests for the Go services (113 test files) and documented each system for handover.
Built Tanya Data, an AI assistant that answers questions about sales, stock and receivables from BigQuery (see Projects).
work.summary: Full-time. Started as an IT intern (Jul - Sep 2026). Responsible for the Odoo-Accurate integration, the HR and recruitment system, the inventory app and the company OKR system, working directly with finance, warehouse and HR. Tech stack: Python, Go, TypeScript, JavaScript, SQL | Odoo XML-RPC, Accurate Online API, Google BigQuery, Flask, Gin, GORM, React, React Native (Expo), MySQL, PostgreSQL (Supabase), SQLite, Gmail API, Claude and Gemini APIs | Docker, nginx, systemd, Git

work.name: Zuliya Group
highlights: Built and run the group ERP (Laravel 13, PHP 8.3, MySQL): cash requests and approvals, journals, attendance with photo and GPS, leave, assets and field operations. Access is set per module and per region, so each branch can follow its own approval steps.

Built an MCP server that lets Claude read the ERP directly: search documents, see which approval desk is backed up, check server health (disk, backup age, failed jobs) and validate gas meter readings. Also built ZIA, an assistant inside the ERP whose rules the owner can update without code changes.

Connected the ERP to outside services: a Telegram bot for tasks, photo reports and password reset codes (each user links their own account with a one-time code), a cloud fingerprint attendance API, and map lookups for attendance addresses.

Reviewed the ERP's security and fixed what I found: a second login page that skipped the account lockout and leaked staff names; attendance photos and locations that every employee could see; and leave and resignation letters readable by 29 accounts, now only HR.
Hardened the server: security headers and Content-Security-Policy in nginx, verified Telegram webhooks, a protected owner account, and working DKIM so ERP emails stop landing in spam.
Made the slow pages fast: the executive dashboard went from 86.5 s to 6.0 s, and the home page from 200 queries to 49.
Built an OCR pipeline that reads handwritten field forms from phone photos and leaves a field blank rather than guess wrong.
work.summary: Freelance. Sole developer of the group ERP, from building features to running the production server. Tech stack: PHP 8.3, Laravel 13, JavaScript, SQL, Python | MySQL, Blade, Telegram Bot API, Fingerspot API, Claude API, MCP, Tesseract, OpenCV | Linux (Ubuntu) VPS, nginx, systemd, Git

work.name: Optik Rizki Eye Plus
highlights: Built and run the POS and stock system used every day by 78 branches and 83 staff accounts: 56,637 sales and 59,787 payment records since January 2026, with 15,365 frames and 5,957 lens SKUs in stock.
Sales with down payments and later settlement, a list of unpaid notes and printed receipts. Staff pick lenses from the master list by prescription (SPH, CYL, ADD) instead of typing sizes by hand.

Stock: barcode printing and scanning, batch and Excel imports, warehouse dispatch, and branch-to-branch shipments that only move stock when the receiving branch confirms, with PDF delivery notes and a full movement trail.
Reports for the owner: revenue per branch and period, analytics with Excel export, and staff bonuses pulled from Google Sheets; per-user permissions and branch management.
Moved price lookup to the server after finding invoices saved at zero when the browser failed to send the price, and fixed a soft-delete bug that hid 289 lens units from stock.
Fixed delivery notes that took 20.7 s and timed out; the cause was a blocked outside request for the QR image. Now 0.04 s.
